bullets.text: Hurricane Katrina caused nearly 30,000 claim reports, over 24,000 incurred claims, and an expected $185M loss (~5.5 times previous record); over 90% resolved by October end; expects to crush over 5,000 vehicles.

Q3 combined ratio was 90.4, with moving parts including favorable frequency, reduced post-Katrina claims activity nationwide, hurricane losses from Katrina and Rita, and $93.9 million in favorable prior-year reserve development.

YTD Personal Lines PIF +10% (Drive auto +6%, Direct auto +12%, special lines +14%), down from 11% in Q2; Commercial Auto PIF +12%, down from 13%; results met company expectations relative to the market.
Q3 NPW +5% and NPE +6%, slightly slower than YTD 7% for both, signaling continued slowing; YOY premium per application down about 5% for Drive auto and 2% for Direct.

$93.9M in favorable prior-year reserve development reflected lower-than-estimated claim severity on closed claims and unresolved claims; claims frequency remained favorable nationwide, with reduced activity the week post-Katrina.

Company rejects viewing large reserve adjustments as "favorable," striving for accuracy at all times; closely monitors frequency and severity trends; advises investors that accident-year loss/LAE ratio best indicates current performance.
Direct channel Internet-initiated business rose ~5% above prior 50%–55% range versus phone; online sale completions without call center transfer also increased by ~5% above prior 60%–65% range.

Reentered New Jersey on September 30, offering personal auto via Drive and Progressive Direct; plans to introduce Commercial Auto products later in 2005, followed by motorcycle and boat products in 2006.
Third quarter consumer shopping activity continued to reflect soft market conditions across the auto insurance industry, characterized by prices experiencing more downward movement than increases.

Viewed individually, Drive Insurance and Progressive Direct each rank in the top ten of all auto writers nationally; both brands entered New Jersey on September 30, officially welcomed by the Acting Governor.
